connection_condition: A consumption record is attributed to exactly one customer through the customer identifier carried on the consumption ledger.
description: A customer's recorded activity is composed of monthly consumption records; a consumption quantity has no meaning without the customer it belongs to.

connection_condition: A transaction is attributed to exactly one paying customer through the customer identifier carried on the transaction ledger.
description: A customer's purchase activity is composed of individual card transactions; a transaction cannot exist without a paying customer.

connection_condition: A transaction is attributed to exactly one station through the station identifier carried on the transaction ledger.
description: The purchase activity recorded at a station is composed of the transactions made there; a transaction occurs at one station and is meaningless without it.

connection_condition: A transaction is attributed to exactly one product through the product identifier carried on the transaction ledger.
description: A transaction is composed of a purchase of one product; the purchased item is identified by the product dimension.

connection_condition: A station carries one chain identifier, and many stations share the same chain identifier.
description: A chain is composed of the stations that operate under it; a station's chain membership is recorded on the station itself.

connection_condition: The day and the clock time of a transaction are both held as separate attributes of the transaction row.
description: The moment of a transaction is a component of the transaction record and cannot be read independently of it.

connection_condition: Monthly consumption totals are aggregated over the analysed scope and the greatest month is selected.
description: The peak consumption month is derived from monthly consumption by taking the month with the largest aggregated consumption within the period.

connection_condition: Monthly consumption values recorded within a year are averaged for the analysed scope and related to the twelve months of that year.
description: Average monthly consumption is derived from the monthly consumption values of a year rather than stored as its own quantity.

connection_condition: Annual consumption of a set of customers is summed and divided by the number of customers in that set.
description: Annual average consumption is derived by normalising the total annual consumption of a customer set by the size of that set.

connection_condition: Annual consumption totals of two consecutive years are compared for the analysed scope.
description: The percentage increase in consumption is derived from the annual consumption totals of two years rather than stored directly.

connection_condition: Indirect: both ledgers carry the same customer identifier, so the two activity streams can be related per customer, but they differ in grain, time coverage and measured quantity and no row-level correspondence exists.
description: Metered gas consumption and station card transactions are two independently recorded views of the same customer base; they are related through the shared customer identifier but describe different phenomena at different grains.

connection_condition: Both are attributes carried on the same customer row, so any cross-tabulation of segment and currency is available at customer grain.
description: Segment and settlement currency are two customer attributes that the workload combines when comparing consumption across segments within one currency.

connection_condition: Not equivalent: the consumption ledger holds a six-character year-month period while the transaction ledger holds a calendar day plus a separate clock time, so the two temporal encodings are not interchangeable and share no comparable value form.
description: Both ledgers express when activity happened, but they record time at different granularities and in different encodings, which makes the shared column name a discovery hazard rather than a join key.
